question: Under Akbar, who was responsible for revenue and financial supervision across the entire Mughal Empire?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Diwan-i-Kul**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Diwan-i-Kul** was the head of the revenue department and financial administration during Akbar's reign, responsible for supervising fiscal matters across the empire.
 
• The position of Diwan-i-Kul was integral in implementing Akbar’s **centralized administration system**, ensuring efficient collection and regulation of revenue.
 
• Under Akbar's reforms, the Diwan-i-Kul played a key role in maintaining accounts related to **taxation, land revenue, and expenditure**.
 
• This office was established as part of Akbar’s **revenue reforms**, which were based on meticulous surveys and assessments conducted under the guidance of Raja Todar Mal.
 
• The Diwan-i-Kul worked alongside other administrative officials to ensure equitable distribution of resources and transparency in financial matters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Raja Todar Mal**: Akbar’s finance minister, who introduced the **revenue system** known as "Zabt" or the land revenue system, which was based on careful measurement and classification of agricultural land.
 
• **Zabt System**: A revenue system that categorized land into different types based on fertility and productivity, ensuring fair taxation.
 
• **Mansabdari System**: A bureaucratic structure introduced by Akbar, where officials were ranked based on their responsibilities and salaries, closely tied to the revenue system supervised by the Diwan-i-Kul.
 
• : Akbar’s governance model was highly centralized, with the Diwan-i-Kul acting as a vital cog in managing the empire’s financial affairs.
 
• Akbar’s revenue reforms were inspired by earlier practices but refined under Todar Mal’s guidance, making them more efficient and equitable for the empire’s subjects.
